memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The priest is to put some of the oil remaining in his palm on the lobe of the right ear of the one to be cleansed, on the thumb of their right hand and on the big toe of their right foot, on top of the blood of the guilt offering. The rest of the oil in his palm the priest shall put on the head of the one to be cleansed and make atonement for them before the LORD." - Lev 14:17-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Read those four words carefully: on top of the blood.

The oil does not go on bare skin. It goes exactly where the blood was already placed. Same ear, same thumb, same toe. Blood first, then oil.

That order is never reversed in Scripture, and it is worth pausing over. Throughout the Bible, oil is linked with anointing and with the Spirit's presence. And the Spirit is never poured out on the unatoned. Forgiveness comes first; empowering follows.

Peter said it plainly at Pentecost: Repent and be baptised... for the forgiveness of your sins. And you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit (Acts 2:38). First the cleansing that Christ purchased, then the Spirit who fills.

Many believers get this backwards. We seek power, experience, or usefulness while leaving unconfessed sin untouched. Or we chase spiritual feeling as a substitute for dealing honestly with God.

But notice also where the rest of the oil goes: on the head. Poured out generously, running down. This is not a stingy dab. The person who had nothing is now anointed like a king.

Blood, then oil. Forgiven, then filled. That is God's order, and it is a generous one.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you seeking God's power while avoiding His cleansing?
2. What unconfessed thing might be standing in the way?
3. What does it mean to you to be forgiven and then generously filled?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, cleanse me first by the blood of Christ, and then fill me with Your Spirit. Let me never seek Your power while avoiding Your searching. Amen.
